pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: light red, film-coated, oval biconvex tablet

tell: It inhibits DPP-4 but not DPP-8 or DPP-9 in vitro, and accumulates minimally on repeated dosing.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is approximately 100%, and a high-fat meal does not significantly change exposure. About 20% is bound to plasma proteins, and 60% to 71% of the dose is excreted unchanged in urine.
A benzoate salt whose active moiety has molecular weight 339.4. A crystalline powder that is sparingly soluble in water.
Marketed under an NDA in 6.25, 12.5 and 25 mg strengths.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated after serious hypersensitivity to it or its excipients; anaphylaxis, angioedema and severe skin reactions have been reported.
Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes.
Selectively inhibits DPP-4, slowing the breakdown of incretin hormones such as GLP-1; in vitro, DPP-8 and DPP-9 are not inhibited.
The generic name begins with A and has ten letters.
